title: Decompose affinity strategies and introduce async decision cache
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The smart-routing layer currently mixes multiple regional affinity strategies (latency-first, cost-first, and capacity-fallback) inside a single evaluator module. This has led to fragile conditionals, duplicated metric instrumentation, and unpredictable tail latency when the system scales or when regional capacity rapidly fluctuates. Goals: 1) Split affinity strategies into small, testable adapters with a shared, minimal decision contract. 2) Replace the hot synchronous decision cache with an asynchronous, bounded cache that pre-warms likely decisions and emits fewer blocking RPCs on the critical path. 3) Reduce tail p95/p99 route-selection latency by 15–25% and eliminate a client-visible class of transient 504s during bursty regional failovers.

Scope and approach: - Introduce a lightweight AffinityAdapter interface (decision input: route context id, constraints, hint tokens; output: candidate route set + scoring metadata). Keep the returned shape intentionally minimal so adapters remain decoupled. - Implement three adapters as separate modules: latency-adapter, cost-adapter, and capacity-adapter. Each adapter runs its evaluation asynchronously and can attach advisory scores. - Build an AsyncDecisionCache that stores recent decision blobs keyed by stable routing input hash. Cache entries are refreshed by background workers and optionally pre-warmed for VIP customers. The on-hotpath lookup returns either a ready decision or a "deferred token" which allows the router to continue with a safe default and merge adapter results as they become available. - Add an experimental fan-in collector that merges late adapter scores and triggers a lightweight re-eval for long-running requests (configurable by host header). - Feature-flag the async cache and new adapters behind routing.feature.async_decision_cache and routing.feature.adapterized_affinity. Trade-offs considered: - Synchronous cache (current system) is simpler but causes head-of-line blocking and amplifies transient RPC failures. - Fully asynchronous routing increases complexity (ordering, eventual consistency) but reduces blocking on the hot path and enables pre-warming. - We avoid heavy-weight transaction semantics for decision updates to keep latency guarantees; instead we rely on conservative defaults plus monitored divergence metrics.

Metrics and success criteria: - Target: reduce route-selection p95 by >=15% and p99 by >=10% for the largest shard during peak. - Reduce route-selection RPCs per request by 30% via cache hits. - Add new metrics: decision_cache.hit_ratio, decision_cache.deferred_rate, adapter.latency.{latency,cost,capacity}.

Review and rollout plan: 1) Prototype module-level adapters behind flags and run integration tests in staging (current). 2) Deploy AsyncDecisionCache to a single region with canary traffic (5% of routing requests). 3) Expand to 25% and monitor divergence and re-eval rates. 4) Full rollout if metrics meet success criteria and SRE signoff.

Documentation: design notes and sequence diagrams are in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RND/Async+Decision+Cache+Design. Initial implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5421.
comments: 2025-01-30 - Spike complete: implemented a proof-of-concept async cache with background refresher; measured warm-hit latency of ~0.8ms and cold path median added latency ~4.1ms.
2025-02-03 - Architecture review with SRE and Runtime teams: requested clearer invariants for 'safe default' behavior and an emergency circuit that disables async merges if re-eval churn > 0.5%.
2025-02-07 - Design update: switched cache key to stable routing hash (includes model id, region hints, and user-configured affinity override) per runtime feedback to reduce invalidation storms.
2025-02-10 - PR 5421 submitted for adapter interfaces and async cache core. Unit tests added for adapter failure modes. Seeking two approvals (L. Patel, S. O'Neill).

2025-02-12 - Load test in staging: p95 route-selection latency on canary fell from 18ms to 14.8ms (18% improvement). Observed a new class of late adapter merges that caused a small number of duplicate route-selection events; adding idempotency tokens to mitigates double-eval side-effects.

2025-02-14 - Blocker: third-party dependency 'shardmap' at v2.1.0 has a regression with concurrent reads causing occasional stale shard metadata. Mitigation: pin to v2.0.4 and open ENG-42901 to track upstream upgrade.
